messages:
anya: PR opened with tenant threshold examples for the provisioning playbook — https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4567. Aim: clarify autoscale vs. burst thresholds and show a short CLI example for tenant admins. Can the docs team eyeball?

sam: taking a look today. do we want separate YAML examples for reserved pools vs burst policies?

anya: yes — two compact samples. one for a 'reserved-pool' commit (predictable capacity), one for 'burst' with cooldown and preemption note. also need a short SLA impact blurb.

marta: quick nit — in the YAML field name `threshold_pct` feels ambiguous. propose `target_utilization_pct` to match autoscale schema used elsewhere.

kevin: sgtm. also adding a one-line SDK snippet idea showing how to set `tenant_label` during provisioning. quick paste: 

```yaml
# burst policy example (draft)
policy:
  type: burst
  threshold_pct: 75
  cooldown_s: 300
  tenant_label: "team-alpha"
```

kevin: updated suggestion to be consistent: 

```yaml
policy:
  type: burst
  target_utilization_pct: 75
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  tenant_label: "team-alpha"
```

marta: also add a short note: burst pools are preemptible and may be evicted under capacity pressure — link to eviction model: https://internal.redwood/docs/eviction-model (one sentence, inline).

anya: can someone add a small CLI snippet for tenant admins to set the policy? e.g.

```bash
redwoodctl capacity set-policy --tenant team-alpha --policy burst --target 75 --cooldown 300
```

sam: i'll add the CLI snippet + a tiny smoke unit test to the PR. i'll also write a 2-line sidebar on SLA tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

docs-bot: Reminder: docs style guide — use present tense, short imperative sentences. Keep examples < 20 lines and add param doc links. :memo:

anya: thanks all. sam + marta, ping when you push edits and i'll merge. tagging @kevin for SDK snippet follow-up. closing loop after review.
